name: The Debt Comes Due
theme: Civilization before conflict; the player is catalyst, not savior.

stages.title: Two Children by the Stream
stages.description: A Stonefang goblin child and a human child play beside a stream until fighting erupts in the distance. Each runs home to a frightened community.

objectives.description: Travel to the human frontier camp and Stonefang.

steps.text: You follow the children back toward two communities living an uneasy day's walk apart, both bracing for a war neither truly wants.

stages.title: Grievances on Both Sides
stages.description: Explore the Stonefang settlement and the frontier camp. Meet Chieftain Grakkor and Captain Thomas Rourke; gather reports, testimony, maps and evidence.

objectives.description: Gather evidence of the true cause.

nodes.speaker: Chieftain Grakkor
nodes.text: Human blades were seen near our watering stones. My people bury children while yours count cattle. Why should I trust another outsider?

choices.label: I came to listen, not to judge. Tell me what your scouts saw.
[Cultural] Offer the Stonefang stoneword of parley before speaking.
Your warriors may have struck first. I need the truth.

nodes.speaker: Chieftain Grakkor
nodes.text: You see clearly. Neither side struck first with intent. Something drove the beasts and the lost ones toward us both.

choices.label: Then we may still stop this.

nodes.speaker: Chieftain Grakkor
nodes.text: Corrupted things move at the treeline. My veteran Skarn lost his mate to them and now sees only human faces to blame.

choices.label: I will weigh every account before I speak.

nodes.speaker: Captain Thomas Rourke
nodes.text: I am practical, stranger. I lost good people. I do not want a war, but I will not leave my camp undefended on a promise.

choices.label: Then let us find the truth together, honestly.
[Diplomacy] Both your peoples are being hunted by the same enemy.

nodes.speaker: Captain Thomas Rourke
nodes.text: You reason like someone who has buried people of their own. If the goblins will meet, I will listen.

nodes.speaker: Captain Thomas Rourke
nodes.text: Bring me proof of a common enemy and I will consider standing down.

steps.prompt: You examine tracks, wounds and torn maps around both camps.

on_failure.text: The signs are muddled, but a pattern of corruption lingers at the edges.

steps.prompt: A Stonefang elder offers to teach you the customs of parley. Do you take the time?

options.label: Learn the Stonefang customs of parley.
There is no time; move to the negotiation.

stages.title: The Long Table
stages.description: Conversation-driven diplomacy. Both sides present legitimate grievances. Preparation shapes what is possible; speech supports it rather than replacing it.

objectives.description: Broker an understanding between Grakkor and Rourke.

steps.text: Grakkor and Rourke sit at opposite ends of a plank table. Their grieving veterans, Skarn and Halden, stand behind them like mirrored shadows.

steps.prompt: How do you open the negotiation?

options.label: Mediate: name the corruption as the true enemy of both peoples.
Pressure both sides to disarm immediately.

steps.prompt: You press for a lasting agreement.

on_success.text: Grakkor sets his axe flat on the table. Rourke, after a long breath, does the same.

on_failure.text: No embrace, but a fragile truce holds: enough to face what is coming.

stages.title: The Corruption Breaks the Truce
stages.description: A major Corruption attack interrupts the talks. Corrupted wildlife and lost civilized folk assault both camps. Humans and goblins must fight as one.

objectives.description: Repel the corrupted assault on the camps.

steps.text: Horns. Screaming. The treeline vomits corrupted beasts and hollow-eyed people who were once farmers and hunters. There is no time left to argue.

waves.name: The lost ones surge the gate
A corrupted alpha leads the charge

stages.title: Hold the Line
stages.description: The civilians can escape only if someone holds the breach.

objectives.description: Decide how the civilians will escape.

steps.prompt: The civilians are fleeing. What do you do?

options.label: Stay behind with Grakkor and Rourke to hold the line yourself.
Organize the retreat and let the veterans hold.

steps.text: Skarn and Halden, the two grieving veterans, fight back to back against the corruption. Grief becomes, for one moment, a shared cause.

stages.title: The Caravan to a New Home
stages.description: Stonefang warriors escort the refugee caravan to Talos's multicultural hometown. Several volunteers choose to remain and help build the settlement.

objectives.description: See the refugee caravan safely to Talos's hometown.

steps.text: Under a Stonefang escort, the caravan winds toward Talos's hometown -- a settlement already known for welcoming strangers.
At the gates, a handful of Stonefang volunteers lay down their war-paint and take up mason's tools. They mean to stay.
